title: Barn Owls Make a Surprise Home in Manhattan
summary:
A family of barn owls has moved into a water tower on top of a building in Manhattan, in New York City. The building is on West 75th Street, close to Central Park.

Andrew Farnsworth, a bird scientist at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, says this is the first time barn owls are known to have nested in Manhattan in recorded history.

A neighbor named Elisabeth Williams told a local news outlet about the owls on October 6. A birder named David Barrett says he has seen at least one adult owl and five young owls, called fledglings.

Barn owls are very rare in New York City parks. Now crowds gather every night hoping to see them. Neighbors had heard loud screeching at night since September. That screech is how barn owls talk to each other. "I think we're about to become birders," Williams said.
why_it_matters: Even in a big city, wild animals can find homes, and kids can watch and learn about them.
